result.title: From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation
result.summary: Visually evoked EEG-to-text generation aims to produce natural-language descriptions from neural responses elicited by visual stimuli. Existing approaches typically compress EEG signals into a single global representation and directly project it into the hidden space of a large language model (LLM), which may limit the preservation of complementary visual semantics under noisy and subject-dependent EEG signals. We propose a dual-view semantic token bridging framework that exploits raw images and sketch images as complementary visual supervision to learn raw-oriented and sketch-oriented EEG semantic token streams. To interface these structured neural representations with an LLM, we introduce a branch-specific semantic query bridge that aggregates each token stream into compact semantic slots and converts them into LLM-compatible soft prompts. A progressive adaptation strategy further transitions the learned visual-semantic interface from image-supported training to image-free EEG-conditioned generation. Experiments demonstrate strong subject-wise EEG classification performance and competitive EEG-to-text generation across multiple LLM backbones. Ablation, branch-level representation, and EEG-label disentanglement analyses further show that the two EEG streams learn complementary view-oriented representations and that EEG-derived prompts provide sample-specific information beyond category labels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出双视角 EEG 语义 token 桥接框架：以原始图像和素描图像作为互补视觉监督，学出两路 EEG 语义 token 流，再经分支特定的语义查询桥聚合成紧凑语义槽并转为 LLM soft prompt，并用渐进适应从有图训练过渡到无图 EEG 条件生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 训练期借视觉监督、推理期去掉图像的做法类似 LVR 中的视觉旁路问题，语义槽压缩加 soft prompt 注入，以及「EEG 提示是否携带类别标签之外信息」的分析，可供核查条件表示的信息坍缩与答案是否真正使用 latent 内容。
